chapter_name: Poems by Blake (The Divine Image & The Human Abstract) by William Blake
learning_objective: 🎯 Contrast William Blake's two states of the human soul: the innocent divine qualities of mercy and love versus the corrupt, selfish institutions created by human intellect!

main_concepts.concept_title: 💖 The Divine Image (From Songs of Innocence)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Blake praises the four virtues: Mercy, Pity, Peace, and Love. He argues that God and humans are connected because these virtues exist within the human heart—wherever these virtues are shown, God is present.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🐍 The Human Abstract (From Songs of Experience)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: A direct counterpart/critique to 'The Divine Image'. Blake shows how human selfishness twists those virtues: we only have 'Pity' because we allow poverty to exist, and 'Mercy' because we create misery.
In 'The Human Abstract', cruelty, fear, and deceit grow into a metaphorical tree inside the human brain. It bears the poisonous fruit of Deceit and feeds on hypocrisy.
Blake demonstrates that humanity has a dual nature: capable of divine compassion, yet equally capable of rationalizing cruelty and institutionalizing suffering.

fun_activity.title: ⚖️ The Two-Sided Coin
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a tree on paper. On the left side (Innocence), label the leaves with positive virtues like kindness and honesty. On the right side (Experience), write what happens when those virtues are faked for selfish gain.

exam_tips: 📌 Always compare the two poems together—they represent Blake's 'two contrary states of the human soul'.
📌 In 'The Human Abstract', explain that the gods search for the Tree of Mystery in nature, but fail because it grows only inside 'the Human Brain'.
📌 Remember that Blake strongly criticized religious institutions that preached moral rules while ignoring social injustice and poverty.
quick_recap: ⭐ 'Mercy, Pity, Peace, and Love' are described as God's divine body in man.
⭐ 'The Human Abstract' argues that society artificially creates suffering just so people can act charitable.
⭐ Blake used simple, ballad-like rhythms to convey profound philosophical and social criticism.
